extracted.intended_audience: systematic reviewers and health technology assessment researchers (readers of HTA appendices)
extracted.subtask_description: Appendix listing and summarising empirical studies from the grey literature for a systematic review / meta-analysis, including study design, sample sizes, outcomes, effect estimates and quality/bias information. Used to assess grey-literature-related bias in pooled estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grey literature bias – included empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Header/section title used to identify and present empirical studies drawn from grey literature that were included in the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the included grey-literature empirical studies and summarises their characteristics and results (e.g. sample sizes, outcomes, effect estimates). The appendix explicitly groups material under 'Grey literature bias – included empirical studies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify each study by design (e.g. randomised controlled trial, non-randomised, case–control, cohort, before–after, cross‑sectional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables/notes in the appendix distinguish studies by design and use that classification when presenting effect estimates and discussing bias (the document repeatedly lists designs such as 'randomised', 'non-randomised', 'case–control', 'cohort').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sample size for each study
rubrics_metrics.description: Each study entry should include the sample size (number of participants) and sometimes subgroup counts or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix tables present sample sizes alongside estimates and use sample sizes when interpreting precision; sample size is a required descriptive field for included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report outcome effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals and p-values
rubrics_metrics.description: Present point estimates of effect (e.g. RR/OR/mean difference) accompanied by 95% confidence intervals and p-values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix repeatedly reports estimates with 'I C % 5 9' (OCR of '95% CI') and p-values; reviewers should extract point estimate + 95% CI (and p) for meta-analysis and bias assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report timing / follow‑up duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the time of measurement or follow‑up duration for outcome assessment (e.g. months or years since intervention or baseline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include follow‑up periods or timing of measurement for outcomes; timing is used to compare and pool results appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report participant/population characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe key population characteristics (e.g. mean age, demographic or clinical features, setting) for each study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix entries include baseline/population descriptors (age, study setting, sample representativeness) that inform applicability and heterogeneity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify source type within grey literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the grey‑literature source type for each included item (conference abstract, thesis, letter, report, technical report, government document, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes and the appendix emphasise that data may be from conference abstracts, letters, theses or other non‑peer‑reviewed sources and track source type as part of bias evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for study quality / risk of bias (selection, confounding, reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and note aspects of internal validity such as selection bias, confounding, non‑response, incomplete reporting and whether analyses were adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix tables and text flag non‑randomised designs, potential confounding and incomplete reporting; reviewers are expected to consider these when interpreting results from grey literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish adjusted vs unadjusted effect estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether reported effect estimates are adjusted for confounders or are crude/unadjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and annotations refer to adjusted analyses in some entries; meta‑analysts should prefer adjusted estimates where appropriate and note adjustment status when pooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent statistical reporting categories/thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply and report standard thresholds/categories for statistical significance and precision (e.g. p<0.05, p between 0.05–0.1, CI crossing null).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix shows p‑value and CI reporting and uses these for interpretation; consistent categorisation aids cross‑study comparison and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document outcome definition and measurement method
rubrics_metrics.description: For each study, record how the outcome was defined and measured (definition, diagnostic criteria, measurement instruments or data source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix emphasises heterogeneity in outcome ascertainment across studies (different definitions/measurements) which must be recorded and considered in synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record temporal and contextual details of data source
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when and where the data were collected (dates, location, clinical context) for assessing relevance and potential temporal/contextual bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix entries include dates/periods and settings (e.g. hospital/community) — important for judging applicability and changes in practice over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag incomplete or abbreviated reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify studies with limited reporting (e.g. conference abstracts, short reports) and treat their reported results with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix explicitly contains short-format grey‑literature items; such items often lack methodological detail and should be appraised cautiously or subjected to sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarise heterogeneity and applicability concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary for each study noting factors likely to contribute to heterogeneity (design, population, outcome, measurement) and limitations to applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix structure groups study characteristics and comments so reviewers can quickly identify sources of between‑study heterogeneity and external validity issues.
